حِكٌّ (tropical:) Doubt (K, TA) in religion &c.; (TA;) as also ↓ حِكَّةٌ : (AA, TA:) because it makes an impression (يَحُكُّ) upon the mind. (TA.) ＝
-A2- حِكُّ شَرٍّ, explained in the K, as also شَرٍّ ↓ حِكَاكُ , by the words يُحَاكُّهُ كَثِيرًا, means (tropical:) A producer of much evil, or mischief: (TK:) it is a tropical phrase: and in like manner one says حِكُّ ضِغْنٍ (tropical:) [a producer of much rancour, malevolence, malice, or spite]: and حِكُّ مَالٍ (tropical:) [a producer of much wealth]. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
